context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid Modern Claims Platform built on Azure that incrementally replaces a 30-year-old on-premise mainframe system. Its core purpose is to modernize customer submissions and adjuster workflows while keeping the legacy COBOL/DB2 system as the system of record.

## Key Elements
* Modern Claims Platform (Azure Container Apps / PaaS)
* Mainframe Claims System (IBM z/OS, COBOL, DB2)
* Hybrid Integration Gateway (Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS, IPsec VPN)
* Azure Service Bus & Azure API Management (APIM)
* Corporate Active Directory
* External Payment Gateway
* External Actors: Customers, Brokers, and Claims Adjusters

## Relationships
* Customers and Brokers interact with the Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS / TLS 1.3 (R-01).
* Adjusters utilize the Modern Claims Platform web application with asynchronous caching to meet <2s load times (R-02, R-05).
* The Modern Claims Platform synchronizes data with the Mainframe Claims System via Azure Service Bus and Hybrid Integration Gateway.
* The platform authenticates users against Corporate Active Directory using OIDC / OAuth2 (R-07).
* The platform integrates with the External Payment Gateway for automated claim payouts.

## Technology Stack
* Azure West Europe: Cloud provider region hosting the modern microservices architecture.
* Azure Container Apps / PaaS: Compute platform for running the modern claims web applications.
* Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging to decouple cloud services from the mainframe batch window constraints.
* Azure API Management (APIM) & Azure Key Vault: Secure API gateway proxy and managed secrets management using Managed Identities.
* ExpressRoute, mTLS, IPsec: Hybrid networking and transport security protocols bridging Azure and on-premise infrastructure.
* IBM z/OS, COBOL, DB2: Legacy on-premise system of record.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture allows gradual, risk-managed migration of claim types one-by-one while insulating the constrained mainframe from real-time traffic spikes. Asynchronous messaging and managed Azure services mitigate the team's limited cloud experience while guaranteeing data consistency and strict one-day rollback capabilities.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native platform on Azure. It ensures continuous hybrid operations while migrating claim types incrementally over a three-year period.

## Key Elements
* Claims Web Application (React, TypeScript)
* API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (.NET Core)
* Claims Processing Service (.NET Core, Azure Container Apps)
* Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Functions, Azure Service Bus)
* Claims Database (Azure SQL)
* Configuration & Feature Store (Azure App Configuration)
* Security & Observability (Azure Key Vault, Azure Monitor, Azure WAF)

## Relationships
* Users to Claims Web Application via HTTPS/JSON
* Claims Web Application to API Gateway/BFF via HTTPS/JSON (OIDC/JWT)
* API Gateway/BFF to Claims Processing Service and Configuration Store via HTTPS/gRPC
* Claims Processing Service to Claims Database via TDS/SQL
* Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer to Mainframe via mTLS/AMQP

## Technology Stack
* Frontend: Azure Static Web Apps with React for fast client-side rendering
* Backend & Compute: .NET Core on Azure Container Apps and Azure Functions for scalable business logic
* Database: Azure SQL with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) for structured claim data
* Messaging & Integration: Azure Service Bus with AMQP for asynchronous hybrid synchronization
* Security: Azure Active Directory (Entra ID), Azure Key Vault, and Azure WAF for robust protection
* Configuration: Azure App Configuration for dynamic feature flagging and routing

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture decouples modern sub-second user experiences from slow mainframe responses while preserving the system of record. It satisfies strict fallback and consistency requirements through an asynchronous Anti-Corruption Layer and managed Azure components tailored for a team with limited cloud experience.

Claims Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
Modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform via a hybrid architecture while preserving the COBOL/DB2 mainframe system of record. The Claims Web Application delivers a high-performance, secure, and accessible interface for customers, brokers, and adjusters.

## Key Elements
- Claims Web Application (Azure Static Web Apps, React, TypeScript)
- Routing & Shell Component (React Router, WCAG 2.1 AA)
- Authentication Client Component (MSAL.js, memory-only token storage)
- Claim Submission Feature Component (React Hook Form, Zod, local storage persistence)
- Adjuster Workspace Component (TanStack Query for aggressive caching)
- API Client Component (Axios, Application Insights integration)
- API Gateway / BFF (.NET Core)
- External Systems: Mainframe Claims System, Corporate Active Directory (Entra ID), Azure WAF, Azure Monitor / Application Insights

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker / Claims Adjuster -> Claims Web Application: Interacts via [HTTPS / JSON]
- Claims Web Application -> API Gateway / BFF: Authenticates and sends API requests via [HTTPS / OIDC/JWT]
- Claims Web Application components -> Azure Monitor / Application Insights: Telemetry streaming via [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Serverless hosting providing global CDN and integrated staging slots for rapid fallback deployments.
- React & TypeScript: Component-based UI framework ensuring type safety and maintainable frontend code.
- TanStack Query: Client-side data caching engine to maintain <2s adjuster screen loads despite slow mainframe responses.
- MSAL.js: Microsoft Authentication Library configured for memory-only token storage to mitigate XSS risks.
- React Hook Form & Zod: Client-side form management and validation.
- Axios: Centralized HTTP client managing API communication and error handling.

## Rationale
This architecture uses client-side caching and resilient form persistence to overcome high mainframe latency and connection drop constraints. Strict security controls, including memory-only token storage and WAF protection, satisfy enterprise compliance standards while accommodating the team's limited cloud experience.

API Gateway / BFF.analysis:
## Overview
[Modern Claims Platform] gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system using a hybrid cloud architecture. The API Gateway / BFF securely routes traffic, manages authentication, and orchestrates phased claim migrations.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / BFF (.NET Core)
- Routing & Proxy Component (YARP)
- Authentication & Authorization Middleware
- Feature Routing & Orchestration Component with local fallback cache
- Context Propagation Middleware
- Rate Limiting & Resilience Component (Polly)
- Azure WAF and Azure Managed Identities

## Relationships
- Claims Web Application -> API Gateway / BFF: HTTPS / JSON (OIDC/JWT)
- API Gateway / BFF -> Claims Processing Service & Integration Layer: gRPC (mTLS, TLS 1.3) with OpenTelemetry trace contexts and metadata headers
- API Gateway / BFF -> Configuration & Feature Store: HTTPS / gRPC with local fallback cache

## Technology Stack
- .NET Core: Chosen for framework consistency and team familiarity despite limited cloud experience
- YARP (Yet Another Reverse Proxy): High-performance routing, load balancing, and canary rollouts
- Azure App Configuration: Dynamic feature flagging for step-by-step claim type migration
- OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor: Distributed tracing across the hybrid cloud boundary
- Azure Managed Identities & Key Vault: Secretless infrastructure and secure credential management

## Rationale
This architecture isolates the complex hybrid migration behind a resilient, secure API gateway that protects legacy constraints while ensuring zero claim loss. Local caching and fallback mechanisms guarantee business continuity during cloud service outages.

Claims Processing Service.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by gradually migrating claim types from a 30-year-old mainframe to an Azure-based cloud environment. It ensures business continuity and data consistency via a hybrid integration pattern during the multi-year transition.

## Key Elements
- **Claims Orchestrator Component**: .NET/C# state machine managing claim lifecycles and idempotency.
- **Claim Type Adapter Component**: Strategy-pattern implementation for isolated feature toggling and rapid rollbacks.
- **Validation & Rules Engine Component**: Evaluates business logic locally before persistence.
- **Idempotency & Outbox Processor Component**: Ensures exactly-once processing and handles circuit breaking during batch windows.
- **Audit Logging Component**: Captures immutable business events using Azure SQL Ledger.

## Relationships
- **Claims Orchestrator** -> **Claim Type Adapter**: Invokes type-specific workflows via In-process C# Interfaces.
- **Claim Type Adapter** -> **Claims Database**: Persists state changes via Entity Framework Core [TDS / SQL].
- **Claims Orchestrator** -> **Idempotency & Outbox Processor**: Persists outbox messages transactionally [In-process / C#].
- **Claims Orchestrator** -> **Audit Logging Component**: Emits audit trails [In-process / C#].
- **Idempotency & Outbox Processor** -> **Claims Database**: Stores deduplication keys [TDS / SQL].

## Technology Stack
- **.NET Core**: Core runtime for business logic and components, chosen for enterprise maturity.
- **Azure Container Apps**: Hosting platform for microservices, simplifying operations for teams with limited cloud experience.
- **Azure SQL with SQL Ledger**: Primary database offering tamper-evident audit logs for regulatory compliance.
- **Azure Service Bus**: Asynchronous messaging backbone handling hybrid sync without blocking core workflows.
- **Azure App Configuration & Key Vault**: Centralized feature toggles for rollbacks and secure secret/PII management.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture uses Clean Architecture principles and an outbox pattern to decouple the modern cloud platform from fragile mainframe dependencies. This isolates high-cost mainframe changes, guarantees sub-second adjuster UI performance, and enables one-day rollbacks per claim type.

level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Claims Processing Service container"
parentContainer:
  name: "Claims Processing Service"
elements:
  - type: "component"
    name: "Claims Orchestrator"
    technology: ".NET/C#"
    description: "State machine managing claim lifecycles and idempotency."

Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid Azure cloud platform. The Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer orchestrates dual-write synchronization, protocol translation, and state routing while protecting the legacy system.]

## Key Elements
- Mainframe Translation Adapter (.NET 8 / Azure Functions)
- Batch Window Throttler (Azure Service Bus)
- Dual-Write Router (.NET Core / Azure Functions with Durable Functions)
- Claim Provenance & Audit Registry (Azure Cosmos DB / Redis / Azure Table Storage)
- Claims Processing Service (.NET Core / Azure Container Apps)
- Mainframe Claims System (COBOL / DB2)

## Relationships
- Claims Processing Service -> Dual-Write Router [gRPC]
- Dual-Write Router -> Claim Provenance & Audit Registry [gRPC / Low-latency read-write]
- Mainframe Translation Adapter -> Claim Provenance & Audit Registry [gRPC]
- Mainframe Translation Adapter -> Mainframe Claims System [mTLS / TCP via ExpressRoute]

## Technology Stack
- .NET 8 / Azure Functions: Provides scalable serverless execution for payload translation and routing logic.
- Azure Service Bus: Queues and throttles messages to respect the strict nightly batch window (23:00-05:00).
- Azure Cosmos DB / Redis / Azure Table Storage: Maintains real-time claim provenance and routing state for rapid fallback (R-06).
- Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities: Secures credentials, handles certificate lifecycle, and enforces least-privilege access.

## Rationale
[This architecture successfully isolates the brittle mainframe via anti-corruption patterns and resilient asynchronous queues, ensuring zero data loss during incremental migrations. It satisfies strict hybrid constraints, security mandates, and the 1-day fallback requirement while bridging low cloud experience through managed services.]

Claims Database.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe claims platform using a hybrid cloud architecture. It gradually migrates claim types to a modern Azure-based platform while maintaining uninterrupted core processing.

## Key Elements
- **Claim Core Store**: Azure SQL with Temporal Tables and Row-Level Security (RLS)
- **Migration Sync Staging**: Azure SQL Staging Tables for batch synchronization
- **Data Access Layer**: Entity Framework Core libraries
- **State Reconciliation Engine**: .NET Claims Processing Service component for idempotent upserts
- **Temporal Audit Dispatcher**: Data Access Layer component for history retention

## Relationships
- **Claims Processing Service -> Data Access Layer**: In-process method calls (`.NET references`)
- **Data Access Layer -> Claim Core Store / Migration Sync Staging**: Executes queries and transactions (`TDS / SQL`)
- **Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Claims Processing Service**: Managed API calls routing all writes to avoid direct database access

## Technology Stack
- **Azure SQL Database**: Relational storage providing Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), Column-Level Encryption (Always Encrypted), and Dynamic Data Masking (DDM) for PII security
- **Entity Framework Core**: ORM for data access and automated migration down-scripts supporting rapid rollbacks
- **Azure Entra ID (Managed Identities)**: Secretless authentication between services and databases
- **Azure Monitor**: Observability platform tracking batch window performance and deadlocks

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the legacy mainframe from modern user workflows while enforcing strict trust boundaries and data consistency. Keeping complex reconciliation logic in the .NET layer rather than database procedures ensures maintainability for a team with limited cloud experience.

Configuration & Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
The Configuration & Feature Store manages dynamic routing and feature flags for the Insurance Claims Modernization platform. It enables gradual claim type migration and rapid emergency rollbacks between the legacy mainframe and the new cloud platform.

## Key Elements
- Feature Flag Manager (Azure App Configuration Feature Management)
- Dynamic Routing Store (Azure App Configuration KV-sets)
- GitOps Deployment Pipeline (Bicep/Terraform with automated JSON schema validation)
- Break-Glass Workflow (Automated emergency PR mechanism for rapid rollbacks)
- API Gateway / BFF (.NET Core)

## Relationships
- API Gateway / BFF -> Feature Flag Manager: Evaluates feature flags [HTTPS / Azure SDK, polling/push via Event Grid]
- API Gateway / BFF -> Dynamic Routing Store: Retrieves endpoint routing maps [HTTPS / Azure SDK]
- Emergency Operators -> Break-Glass Workflow: Triggers instant claim-type fallback [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Configuration: Centralized storage for dynamic feature flags and tenant-specific routing rules supporting instant rollbacks (R-06).
- Azure Managed Identities (Entra ID): Authenticates the API Gateway / BFF without static credentials, enforcing least privilege.
- GitOps Pipeline: Ensures all routing changes and feature toggles are version-controlled, validated via JSON schema, and automatically synced.
- Azure Monitor: Provides business impact telemetry and high-priority security alerting for emergency Break-Glass events.

## Rationale
This architecture balances the requirement for rapid, one-day claim rollbacks with strict security and operational guardrails tailored for a team with limited cloud experience. Utilizing GitOps and managed identities eliminates configuration drift and security risks while enabling seamless phased migration.

Security & Observability.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims system via a hybrid cloud platform while ensuring business continuity. It provides secure online claim submission and adjuster processing while bridging Azure and on-premise components.]

## Key Elements
* Token Validator Component (.NET Core Middleware, OpenID Connect)
* Secret Manager Client (Managed Identities, Azure Key Vault)
* Telemetry Aggregator (OpenTelemetry SDK, gRPC, Azure Monitor)
* Audit Logger Component (.NET Core library, Azure Log Analytics)
* mTLS Termination Proxy (Azure Container Apps Ingress)
* Automated Rotation Service (Azure Event Grid, Azure Functions)

## Relationships
* Users to API Gateway: HTTPS / TLS 1.3
* Token Validator to Azure AD (Entra ID): OpenID Connect / HTTPS
* Secret Manager Client to Azure Key Vault: Managed Identities / HTTPS / REST
* Telemetry Aggregator to Azure Monitor: gRPC / OpenTelemetry
* Azure Container Apps to On-Premise Mainframe: mTLS / HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* .NET Core: For secure, standardized middleware and shared security/observability libraries
* Azure Active Directory (Entra ID): For single sign-on, RBAC, and Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE)
* Azure Key Vault: For centralized secret management and automated credential rotation
* Azure Monitor / Log Analytics: For distributed tracing, metrics, and immutable audit logging
* Azure Container Apps: For hosting cloud containers with native ingress mTLS and local disk buffering

## Rationale
[This architecture secures hybrid claims processing and bridges low cloud experience through managed Azure services and reusable templates. It enforces strict zero-trust and compliance without exceeding the immutable mainframe constraints.]
